title: Decoupling Global Inventory Updates
business: Retailers managing high-volume inventory updates across multiple global warehouses.
problem: Direct synchronous API calls between inventory systems and regional storefronts lead to cascading failures when one region experiences high latency or downtime.
solution: Google Cloud Pub/Sub provides global asynchronous messaging, allowing inventory systems to publish updates to a topic without needing to know the status of downstream subscribers.
steps: Create a Pub/Sub topic to serve as the central message bus for inventory events.
Configure individual subscriptions for each regional storefront application.
Publish inventory change events from the central warehouse system to the topic.
Implement logic in regional storefronts to pull and process messages from their respective subscriptions.
Monitor subscription backlog metrics to ensure regional storefronts are keeping pace with updates.
outcome: Improved system resilience where regional storefronts remain operational even if the central inventory system experiences temporary spikes or maintenance.
limitation: Pub/Sub is an asynchronous system, meaning there is no guarantee of immediate consistency; check the message delivery latency via monitoring tools to ensure it meets business requirements.

questions.question: In Decoupling Global Inventory Updates, why is Pub/Sub used instead of direct API calls?
options: To prevent cascading failures when regional storefronts experience latency.
To ensure immediate synchronous consistency across all global databases.
To replace the need for regional storefront applications entirely.
To increase the cost of maintaining the central inventory system.
questions.explanation: Direct synchronous calls cause failures to propagate; Pub/Sub decouples these systems.
questions.evidence: Direct synchronous API calls between inventory systems and regional storefronts lead to cascading failures when one region experiences high latency or downtime.

questions.question: In Decoupling Global Inventory Updates, what is a primary trade-off of using this asynchronous messaging approach?
options: The system becomes strictly consistent across all regions.
There is no guarantee of immediate consistency, requiring monitoring of delivery latency.
The system requires all subscribers to be online simultaneously to receive messages.
The central inventory system must manage the connection state of every subscriber.
questions.explanation: Asynchronous systems do not provide immediate consistency, so latency must be monitored.
questions.evidence: Pub/Sub is an asynchronous system, meaning there is no guarantee of immediate consistency; check the message delivery latency via monitoring tools to ensure it meets business requirements.
